estimate.scope: First supported-subset self-hosting milestone — defined acceptance met
estimate.completeWhen: The native CLI compiles its complete compiler input, produces byte-identical successive rebuilds and passes native-path qualification.
estimate.excludes: Full upstream compatibility, additional targets and later optimization are separate work.

steps.title: Native compiler CLI
steps.summary: Read source files and imports, then publish a runnable executable without Node at runtime.
steps.nextAction: Preserve rooted IO, typed effects and no-replace publication as optimization proceeds.
design: Command: gleam-native SOURCE.gleam NEW_OUTPUT [--source-root DIRECTORY]. SOURCE is relative to that root, or cwd by default.
Pure Gleam requests drive an owned Linux syscall runner. Resolved constructor fields, label order and callback types are checked before emission.
Rooted regular-file reads refuse source symlinks. Exclusive sibling output, complete writes, fsync and no-replace rename preserve existing paths.
The qualified limit is 128 KiB per source and a 512 MiB compiler arena; ordinary output programs retain 64 MiB. No GC or growth.

acceptance.text: Compile and execute all 16 tracked examples with exact bootstrap byte comparisons.
Run the native CLI with an empty PATH and no external process execution.
Verify real short IO, interrupted/error paths and unchanged existing destinations.
Record input limits, native image hashes and actual ELF dependency checks.

steps.title: Full-size reliability
steps.summary: Measured stack and allocation fixes allow the actual complete compiler source to rebuild.
steps.nextAction: Retain the measured failure frontier; address further stack or memory limits only with evidence.
design: The frozen baseline failure sampled 256 UTF-8 validator frames; only 1.17 MiB of arena was used. Direct returned self-call lowering fixes that causal stack growth.
Arguments are evaluated left-to-right before replacing parameters. Blocks/cases propagate tail context; closures and non-tail calls do not.
Balanced byte merges and reverse closure accumulation remove repeated prefix copies. The earlier 64 MiB and 512 MiB allocation failures remain recorded.
Production: 128 KiB/source, 512 MiB compiler arena; observed self-rebuild allocation 368,525,376 bytes and peak RSS 360,320 KiB. No arbitrary-input or speed claim.

acceptance.text: Record the causal native stack/frame path for a reproducible large-input failure.
Prove bounded-stack loops, dependent/reordered arguments and unchanged non-tail recursion semantics; inspect ASM.
Measure memory behavior and fail without publishing partial output on exhaustion.
Qualify a higher boundary against actual large modules and a representative full graph.

steps.title: Broader native testing
steps.summary: All 371 current positive/negative cases pass through the rebuilt stage-3 native compiler.
steps.nextAction: Expand native and independent upstream comparisons with every language/runtime addition.
design: 729 regression checks and 371 fresh upstream comparisons are separately recorded.
Stage 3 compiles 251 accepted and 120 rejected corpus cases; accepted images match bootstrap bytes and execute correctly.
Rejections must return controlled compiler exits with no output, not signals or runtime failure exits.
Coverage includes modules, generics/recursive data, closures, effects, patterns, Unicode, bytes and direct self-tail calls.

acceptance.text: Run representative positive and negative fixtures through the native file path.
Compare exact outputs and diagnostics where the supported contract requires them.
Exercise multi-module and resource/error behavior; retain an explicit coverage matrix.
Record independent upstream agreement separately from native-path coverage.

steps.title: The self-hosting proof
steps.summary: Two actual native self-rebuilds produce the exact same 637,999-byte compiler image.
steps.nextAction: Keep frozen-input, exact-byte and changed-source controls on future compiler changes.
design: --build-compiler NEW_OUTPUT --source-root ROOT retains the effect runner. All 27 actual compiler modules are read through the native IO path.
Stages 1, 2 and 3 have the same SHA256: 3a8063b7582cb04e53c7443110403dc80f7c757fab0a893add0089a367ca8b65.
The rebuilt image runs --version and qualifies the entire 371-case corpus with empty PATH.
An isolated version-literal change produces a different correct image matching bootstrap. Full upstream compatibility remains false.

acceptance.text: Compile the complete exact compiler input graph through a native self-build command.
Run the rebuilt compiler independently of the stage-0 host.
Produce byte-identical successive compiler images from identical inputs.
Run native-path checks with the rebuilt image and retain the full provenance.

steps.title: Gleam compatibility
steps.summary: Extend language coverage beyond what this compiler currently needs to compile its own source.
steps.nextAction: Select the next construct from a real source need and establish upstream semantic probes first.
design: Remaining areas include general inference, polymorphic function values, selective/package imports and labelled function calls.
Constants, attributes, opaque types, remaining patterns, floats and Unicode operations need bounded, explicit implementations.
Keep unsupported forms explicit; do not turn a growing subset into a claim of full conformance.
Refine each outline when its implementation starts rather than freezing speculative architecture now.

acceptance.text: Define the supported syntax/types/semantics for each increment.
Add independent upstream acceptance and observable-behavior comparisons.
Test scope, inference, evaluation order, errors and relevant emitted instructions.
Update documented compatibility limits without deleting historical failures.

steps.title: Complete value semantics
steps.summary: Finish exact literals, erased generic equality, compound printing and remaining bit-array operations.
steps.nextAction: Choose one real semantic gap and settle its representation before extending accepted inputs.
design: Decimal literal magnitude currently stops at 2^53−1 to retain exact bootstrap representation; native arithmetic remains checked signed 64-bit.
Structural equality works for concrete supported layouts, including recursive values. Stored erased parameters and actual function values remain explicit rejections.
Compound formatting and remaining byte/bit/codepoint forms need owned runtime semantics.
Use an explicit exact representation for larger literals; never round or guess an unknown layout.

acceptance.text: Preserve exact value bits across lexing, checking, emission and execution.
Define representation/type information for any new generic value operation.
Qualify boundary, negative, nested and unsupported cases against upstream where applicable.
Inspect the relevant native instructions and retain overflow/resource behavior.

steps.title: Measured optimization
steps.summary: Measure and improve compilation, generated code, allocations and size after correctness.
steps.nextAction: Profile measured costs before more optimization; extend general pattern/data/indirect boundaries without weakening behavior.
steps.specMaturity: Scalar CFG/calls qualified and benchmarked; general whole-function scope remains
design: Existing instruction inspection and resource fixes are not language-wide performance benchmarks.
Separate cold/warm compilation, runtime execution, allocation/peak memory and artifact-size measurements.
Use multiple runs, retain environment/toolchain/input hashes and report variation.
Select an observed bottleneck, inspect ASM and compare correctness before/after.
Jay requested look-ahead and register spilling. Keep evaluation order and overflow traps; preserve live values across internal calls and Linux syscall RCX/R11 clobbers.
R14/R15 remain reserved arena registers. Internal calls use the owned stack ABI, not an assumed SysV convention. Static instruction counts are not dynamic performance evidence.
The earlier leaf RHS increment eliminated 260 static push/pop pairs and 451 instructions on fixed source; frame traffic remains unchanged. This is not a full allocator or runtime speed claim.
Sibling-arm slots reserve the maximum branch footprint: fixed-source named frame totals fall 36,800 to 26,112 bytes; no peak-stack or speed claim.
Typed integer regions now use explicit register/flags liveness, three-register allocation and nested spills; unmodeled indirect/data boundaries remain.
A seeded 100-expression program agrees with BigInt and upstream; 68 regions spill, maximum operand pressure seven.
Named integer calls now save live pool values before arguments and copy return values before restoration. Calls kill the entire value pool, recovery scratch and Flags.
A separate seeded call program verifies 286 calls and 386 ordered effects. The fixed compiler-source image is unchanged; no broad speedup is claimed.
Scalar comparisons, short-circuit expressions and supported two-arm cases now use successor-aware CFG liveness and real joins.
Repeated benchmarks show no conclusive broad speedup; identical-code controls expose shared-host wall noise. Actual current-source self-build: 8.75 s median wall, 7.42 s CPU, 390.8 MiB peak RSS.

acceptance.text: Publish a reproducible baseline with separate speed, memory and size measures.
Identify the actual hot path rather than infer runtime speed from binary size.
Retain semantic qualification while changing code generation or allocation.
Record measured improvement, regressions and uncertainty on representative workloads.

steps.title: Targets & distribution
steps.summary: Add ARM64/macOS and make qualified native releases convenient to install.
steps.nextAction: Define the next target ABI and executable/runtime contract before implementing it.
design: Current native execution is Linux x86-64 only. ARM64 needs its own emitter/ABI and macOS needs executable-format and syscall/runtime work.
Verify target semantics on the actual target rather than treating ELF output as portable.
Source is in the private GitHub repository; local generated images are excluded from Git.
Release packaging, install/update commands and artifact provenance follow a qualified standalone result.

acceptance.text: Specify calling convention, object/runtime behavior and executable headers for each target.
Execute compiler/output checks on actual target environments.
Publish versioned artifacts with hashes and supported-target/limit declarations.
Verify standalone installation/update behavior without adding runtime dependencies.
